source.summary: GitHub Actions ‘Embedder footprint’ runs for PR #259 (branch fix/258-import-name-match at commit 5451a0dc3e2ac4a5625a0921e1a5760405dc5bcf, whose parent is current main 03352c6b7a81763ac7aa769c40c812ec9db4856f, so the pull-request merge tree is the branch head itself and no merge commit was needed; ubuntu-24.04, Rust 1.96.0): workflow_dispatch runs 45086986197 and 45086998757 against the branch and pull-request run 45085326459, which built the same tree, produced byte-identical sizes for every gated series
source.derivation: Re-baseline for PR #259 (#258, component import lookup applies the #117 NameMap semver rules). The PR generalises crates/telomere-component/src/runtime/name_match.rs (compatible_name / incompatible_name, one shared implementation for export and import names) and routes every import-resolution path in crates/telomere-component/src/linker.rs through a resolve_registered helper (exact match first, otherwise the highest version on the compatible track): root func imports, instance imports, funcs inside an imported instance, and the instance part of a resource drop (the resource name itself stays exact, which also fixes the instance half of #118’s drop path); when only an incompatible version is registered, the error now names both the expected and found versions, in the same format as the #117 export-side error. Attribution was isolated by measuring current main (03352c6) alone (workflow_dispatch run 45087010624, gate success): it reproduces the previous baseline exactly on all 28 gated series, so every delta is this PR’s own. Growth is confined to the configurations that link telomere-component (component, wasi, wasi-threads): release stripped file +10,016..+10,032 B and stripped .text +9,552 B; release-size (opt-level z, fat LTO, one codegen unit) stripped file +4,288..+4,368 B and stripped .text +3,728..+3,808 B. The baseline configuration and every core configuration (core, core-nosimd, core-jit) are byte-identical in both profiles, so 16 of 28 gated series are unchanged and 12 move. Run-to-run spread was again 0 B for every gated series (14 profile/configuration rows x stripped file and stripped .text, n=3; the raw file and .text sizes were also identical across the three runs), so each threshold equals its observed baseline exactly (baseline + 0). Any further growth requires an intentional re-baseline; see docs/benchmarks/footprint.md, ‘Size regression gate (#164)’.
